POC summary / key quotes and CRM fragments:
- Use-case: customer-facing shopping assistant + backend tool-calls (inventory, price check, order-intent). Need deterministic JSON for downstream services.
- Evaluation outcome: quality regression observed when swapping from incumbent (OpenAI) -> major pain in structured output and tool-calling reliability.
- Metrics called out by PM: 'We had 93% parseable order-intents from incumbents, Redwood returned ~71% on same prompts — that delta breaks our orchestration.'
- Tool-calling specifics: malformed args, extra filler text inside JSON blobs, missing required keys (sku, qty). Several failures caused 5 live errors in integration tests.
- SE notes: model devs tuned instruction templates but saw brittle behavior on longer turn histories. Investigated prompt engineering + partial KV caching; improvement but not parity.
- Security: CISO requires SOC2 + KMS/HSM diagram + data residency (EU subset for EU customers). Security review open (see drive/security/attachments/hightower-scan-2026-01).
- Commercial: Hightower's finance put migration on hold (budget freeze) — procurement paused unless clear ROI within 6 months.
- Org/people: internal champion (Elise Ramos) deprioritized; new priority is payment platform overhaul. No clear exec sponsor to push migration.
- Competitor motion: incumbent offered migration assistance + credits; closed deal before Redwood could commit to engineering fixes.
- Recommended next steps logged: 1) Track product fixes for structured-output/tool-calling (SRE/Model teams). 2) Prepare a focused mini-POC showing >90% structured-output pass on canonical set. 3) Re-open in Q3 2026, try to identify new champion.
